correctness.rationale: The deletion condition is exactly pairwise multiset intersection at most one, because a common two-symbol descendant exists iff at least two symbols (with multiplicity) can survive from both. For each heavy word choose a twice-occurring symbol; the chosen symbols are injective across codewords or else their overlap is at least two. Replacing all heavy words by corresponding constant multisets preserves every pairwise intersection bound, and the remaining light words are distinct-symbol n-subsets. These subsets form a 2-(q,n,1) packing, yielding the upper bound q+P. The q constants together with a maximum packing meet the bound exactly. The proof handles n>q, n=q and n=2; the n=3 modular values use independently known maximum partial triple-system leave theorems. Sixteen exact finite ILP comparisons using two different formulations corroborate the theorem without being presented as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The two-survivor channel is the first nontrivial high-deletion multiset coding problem; exact q>=4 behavior when n<=q was left unresolved by the directly relevant 2026 paper. The result is an exact structural equivalence for all alphabets and block lengths, proving that repeated multiplicities never improve capacity over a canonical code made of constants plus classical block packings. It transfers established packing designs and sharp minimum-leave enumerations into all-q exact n=3 coding values, and gives sharp thresholds n>=q. Its content is the non-obvious elimination of repeated-symbol codewords rather than a recomputation of a known table, while no general design-packing solution or encoder is claimed.
